title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. W is a 'basic localizer' (localisateur fondamental) on (Cat), satisfying conditions such as Loc 3. Hot(W) = W^{-1}(Cat). For a small category A, A^ is the category of presheaves on A, W_A = i_A^{-1}(W), and Hot_A = W_A^{-1}A^. The previous page showed two things. First, if A is a local test category, a separating interval I in A^ gives a homotopy structure on A^ compatible with W. Second, W_A is stable under coproducts, f_i in W_A for all i implying ∐f_i in W_A; this reduces to (Cat), where it follows from Loc 3 applied to maps over an index category J.

Corollary 1 (this page). Finite direct sums (coproducts) exist in Hot(W). The canonical functors (Cat) → Hot(W) and A^ → Hot_A → Hot(W) commute with them. For A^, 'on est ramené au cas de (Cat)', because i_A: A^ → (Cat), F ↦ A/F, commutes with coproducts. A marginal note says the finiteness hypothesis is unnecessary, since arbitrary sums are obtained just as directly.

Remark. Let M be a category and W ⊂ Fl(M) admit a calculus of right fractions. Then M → W^{-1}M commutes with finite limits, 'in particular finite sums'. This only makes sense if 'lim' carries an arrow, i.e. inductive limits (colimits); the side convention must match Gabriel–Zisman.

Then a worry. If one works instead with a modified pair (Cat-bar, W-bar), one must check that finite sums, even finite limits, exist there, and that Cat → Cat-bar commutes with them. 'Mais de façon générale…' leads to the next page's Lemma. For a homotopy interval structure on M, with M stable under finite sums and finite sums universal, M → W_h^{-1}M commutes with finite sums. The proof uses that f ~_h g on ∐X_j iff componentwise homotopic, by concatenating intervals I_N uniformly over the finite index set.

Purpose. These are foundational lemmas in the theory of modelizers / test categories (Pursuing Stacks circle). They give additivity properties of the homotopy categories, needed for comparing Hot_A with Hot(W).
errors: Stability of W under coproducts does not by itself imply that the localization functor preserves coproducts. An extra argument is needed (homotopy/interval structure as on the next page, or a calculus of fractions); the page's 'via…' is only a sketch.

The Remark's 'en particulier aux sommes finies' is correct only if 'lim' means inductive limits (colimits) and the side of the fraction calculus is chosen accordingly. Finite projective limits do not include sums.

ideas.what: Hot(W) has (finite, indeed arbitrary) coproducts, and the functors Cat → Hot(W), A^ → Hot_A → Hot(W) preserve them
ideas.modern_name: Coproduct preservation by localization at a basic localizer
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); systematized by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses test categories and Hot; precise statement possibly in Les Dérivateurs context

ideas.what: A localization with a calculus of fractions commutes with finite (co)limits
ideas.where_published: Gabriel–Zisman, Calculus of Fractions and Homotopy Theory

ideas.what: Localization at the homotopy relation of an interval structure preserves finite sums (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy category of a cylinder/interval structure preserves coproducts

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational lemmas on coproducts in localized categories within the test-category/basic-localizer theory. These are well covered by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski.
